title: Personal KPI weekly check-in - Noah Ramirez (2026-03-05)
content:
WEEKLY CHECK-IN (Mar 1- Mar 5, 2026)
Owner: Noah Ramirez
Context: personal tracker for OKRs and short-term KPIs. Quick, messy notes - TODOs + retros.

CURRENT OBJECTIVES + METRICS (top-of-mind)
1) OKR 1 - Reduce inference p95 latency for small-batch hosted endpoints
   - Success metric: p95 latency <= 180ms for 256-token gen on small-batch flows (region: us-west2)
   - This week: 205ms p95 (down from 230ms two weeks ago).
   - Actions taken: enabled smarter batching hint on route /v1/generate (opt-in), tightened max_batch_ms to 8ms for low-latency traffic.
   - Open: need to validate impact on cost (token/sec) and SLO compliance during spikes. TODO: run cost simulation (JIRA-ENG-1543).

2) OKR 2 - Improve eval coverage + regression alerts for core prompt sets
   - Success metric: 95% of critical prompts covered by automated evals; <5% false positives on regression alerts.
   - This week: wrote 12 new eval cases (customer-support + billing flows). Total coverage ~78%.
   - Open: need QA on synthetic labels; ask Sam to review label noise. Link: CONFLUENCE-ENG-4821 (eval design doc).

3) Personal growth KPI - ownership of canary rollout plan for Dedicated launch
   - Deliverable: draft runbook + troubleshooting checklist for on-call to use during canary.
   - This week: first-pass runbook drafted, shared with Maya. Feedback: add rollback checklist and metric thresholds.

BLOCKERS / RISKS
- Metric noise during load tests: synthetic traffic config didn't match prod seq length distribution, skewing p95. Quick fix: update loadgen to sample from production sequence histogram (next week).
- Conflicting priorities: product asked to push a model variant to prod which may change latency profile; need to coordinate rollout windows to avoid metric regression during our test. Action: schedule alignment sync w/ product (owner: Maya).

RETROSPECTIVE NOTES
- What worked: small, frequent changes to batching config gave measurable latency gains without heavy code changes. Rolling these as config toggles is nice.
- What didn't: eval labeling pipeline still manual and slow; this blocks getting automated alerts to high confidence.
- Idea: explore lightweight crowd-labeling for edge cases or add model-based pseudo-labeler to fast-track candidate evals (R&D spike).

NEXT WEEK PLAN (concrete tasks)
- Finish cost simulation for batching changes (JIRA-ENG-1543). Owner: Noah. Due: 2026-03-09.
- Update loadgen to sample seq-length histogram; re-run perf tests. Owner: Noah + infra. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Incorporate Maya's feedback into canary runbook + add rollback checklist. Owner: Noah. Due: 2026-03-08.
- Pair with Sam on eval labeling quality and create an action plan for 3rd-party labeling or pseudo-labeler spike. Owner: Noah + Sam. Due: 2026-03-12.

NOTES TO SELF (scratchpad)
- Quick checklist for perf run:
  * baseline p95 capture (prod window 9-11am PST)
  * deploy batching hint config to staging (tag: batching-opt-2026-03-05)
  * run loadgen with seq-hist sample 10x, capture traces
  * compare token/sec and GPU utilization
- Slack msg draft to product: "we have a pending model push that may affect latency. Can we gate the push until after our canary window or align on rollback criteria?"

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS
- Does the Dedicated SLA require a different metric threshold for p95 compared to hosted? (ask legal/ops)
- How aggressive can we be with max_batch_ms before customer quality degrades? Need micro-experiment on small subset of customers.

RAW TODOS (quick, actionable)
- [ ] Create JIRA ticket for cost sim (if not existing) - owner: Noah
- [ ] Schedule sync w/ product - owner: Maya
- [ ] Add rollback checklist to runbook - owner: Noah
- [ ] Ping Sam for eval label review - owner: Noah

END
